ov: A large, semi-aquatic rodent of North American wetlands with thick brown fur and a scaly, flattened tail used as a rudder. It lives in families in bank burrows or mounds of vegetation called push-ups, and has become an invasive pest in Europe.

why.et: Eaten in parts of North America; in south-east Michigan Catholics are allowed to eat it on Lenten Fridays.

len: 40–70 cm, about half of it tail
rg: Most of Canada and the US and a small part of northern Mexico; introduced to Europe, northern Asia and parts of South America.
df: About 95% plants, mainly cattails and water lilies, plus mussels, frogs, crayfish, fish and small turtles.
fx: In the Netherlands and Belgium its burrowing damages the dikes that hold back floods.
Royal Canadian Mounted Police winter hats are made from muskrat fur.
